title: MNX Lab vendor extensions (`_x.mnxLab`) — v6.2
description: Everything MNX Lab carries that W3C MNX v19 cannot express: fretted-instrument tablature, chord symbols, and document metadata (what the piece is, and what wrote the file). All of it lives under the single vendor key `_x.mnxLab`, which is how the MNX spec says extensions are namespaced (w3c-cg/mnx#63/#429: the `_x` key identifies an agent, vendor or community). Documents using these extensions remain fully valid against the official MNX schema. Each block is shaped like the standard MNX object it is a draft of, so adopting any of them upstream means deleting the `_x.mnxLab` wrapper rather than rewriting the data. Rationale and the proposals these draft: docs/mnx-extensions.md.

note-id.description: ID of another note in the document (MNX id-reference idiom).

rhythmic-position.description: MNX `rhythmic-position`: a metric position within a measure, as a fraction of a whole note. Same shape and units as `tempo.location` and `segno.location`.

string-number.description: Which string the note is played on — the performer's authoritative CHOICE. String 1 is the highest-pitched string (E4 on a standard-tuned guitar), MusicXML's convention and the opposite of the visual tab convention. Drafts `note.string` (roadmap/proposed/low-priority/spec-instrument-position.md): given the part's string declaration, the capo and the note's sounding pitch, the fret is derived arithmetic.

fret-number.description: Fret number; 0 = open string, counted from the capo when one is declared. OPTIONAL and NON-AUTHORITATIVE: the rendered fret is always derived from string + pitch, and a stored fret's only job is validation — a mismatch with the derived fret is a diagnostic (typically a broken importer), never a rendering input. See roadmap/complete/core-derived-positions.md.

bend-point.description: One control point on a bend curve.

position.description: Where in the note the point falls, as a fraction of the note's own duration (0 = onset, 1 = release).

alter.description: Pitch offset from the written note at this point, in SEMITONES — the unit of MNX `pitch.alter` (2 = a whole-step bend). Non-integers are legal: a quarter-tone curl is 0.5.

technique.description: Playing techniques. Visible in both notation and tab views; none of them require a position, and none is specific to fretted instruments — this block is drafted for standard MNX, not for tab (see docs/mnx-extensions.md §technique).

bend.description: A bend as a CURVE, not a single interval: an ordered list of control points across the note. A pre-bend is a first point at position 0 with a non-zero alter; a release is any later point whose alter decreases. This is how every guitar editor models bends, and it is the deficiency w3c-cg/mnx#63 opens with — MusicXML's single `<bend-alter>` cannot state a bend that rises, releases and rises again.

points.description: In ascending `position` order. The first point should be at position 0.

target.description: Destination note for shift/legato slides. slideIn/slideOut have no target.

hammerPull.description: Hammer-on or pull-off to `target` — ONE adornment, the Soundslice convention (v6): the direction is implicit in the two pitches (up hammers, down pulls), so storing it would be a second spelling of a fact the music already states. Drawn as a letterless slur.

harmonic.description: A harmonic. Identified by TOUCHING PITCH rather than touching fret: that is MusicXML's model, it covers fretless instruments, and it can state the between-fret nodes that w3c-cg/mnx#179 is about, which a fret integer cannot. The stopped position, when there is one, is already stated by the note's `string` (+ derived or stored `fret`).

type.description: MusicXML models only natural/artificial; the rest are Guitar Pro's and have no MusicXML element.

touchingPitch.description: The pitch of the node touched to produce the harmonic. Absent = the consumer derives it from the string and the harmonic type.

palmMute.description: Per-note, matching how Guitar Pro stores it. In standard MNX this should be a span on the part measure with `position` + `end`, like `ottava` — see docs/mnx-extensions.md.

fingering.description: Which finger plays the note. Not tab-specific (kept separable so it can migrate to standard MNX independently).

finger.description: Finger identifier: T, 1, 2, 3, 4 (left hand); p, i, m, a, c (right hand).

note-tab.description: Stored under note._x.mnxLab.tab. Since v5 only `technique` lives here: `string`/`fret`/`fingering` moved flat onto the vendor dict, mirroring the adopted shape they draft (flat on `note` — roadmap/proposed/low-priority/spec-instrument-position.md). `technique` stays until it graduates via a general articulations proposal (roadmap/complete/core-guitar-technique.md).

string-entry.description: One string's declaration. The string number is explicit — array order carries no meaning.

part-tab.description: Stored under part._x.mnxLab.tab. Since v5 only `staffKind` lives here: `strings`/`capo` moved flat onto the vendor dict (drafting flat `part.strings[]`/`part.capo`). Tab-ness is a VIEW declaration — there is no tab clef and no duplicated tab staff; notation and tab are both derived from the same note stream.

staffKind.description: The part's preferred presentation. Consumers may override (e.g. an app's view toggle). If absent, defaults to notation.

harmony-step.description: A chord root or bass note: an MNX `pitch` minus the octave, since a chord symbol names a pitch CLASS.

harmony-degree.description: An added, altered or omitted extension — MusicXML's `<degree>` model, which is proven interchange and hard to improve on.

harmony.description: One chord symbol. Drafts w3c-cg/mnx#109. Structured AND literal: the enum carries the semantics (so it transposes and re-spells), `text` is the display escape hatch for anything the enum cannot say — the same pattern the CG settled on for dynamics in #518. Positioned by `location`, with no duration: a chord lasts until the next one (w3c-cg/mnx#110).

quality.description: camelCase of MusicXML's `kind` vocabulary. `none` is N.C. (no chord); `other` means the symbol is carried only by `text`.

bass.description: Slash-chord bass note, when it is not the root.

text.description: Display override. Present ONLY when the source's literal spelling differs from what a consumer would render from the structure — so most chords carry none.

color.description: Display color for the symbol — the standard's `simple-color` shape, mirrored here because most standard MNX text-bearing objects carry it. Added in v6.1: the renderer honored it before the schema admitted it.

creator.description: One person or body credited with making the work. Drafts MusicXML's `<creator type="…">` and maps to Dublin Core `dc:creator`. A performing `artist` is deliberately NOT a role here — see `work.artist`.

role.description: What they did. Recommended values, matching MusicXML's open `creator type` and MuseScore's metaTags: `composer`, `lyricist`, `arranger`, `transcriber` (Guitar Pro's "Tabber"), `translator`, `editor`, `publisher`. The list is a recommendation, not an enum: an unfamiliar role from another application round-trips verbatim rather than failing validation.

name.description: The name as the source states it. No normalization, no authority linking (w3c/mnx#56 raises both as open questions for the standard object).

work.description: What the piece IS — the metadata every notation format carries and MNX v27 has nowhere for (w3c-cg/mnx#267, w3c/mnx#56). Drafts a standard root-level `work` object, so adoption means deleting the `_x.mnxLab` wrapper. Every field is optional and every value is a plain string: MNX has no formatted text, and printed placement is a layout concern (MusicXML's `<credit>`), never document metadata. Dublin Core mapping is given per field so the standard object can reuse an existing vocabulary rather than invent one.

title.description: The piece's title (`dc:title`). MusicXML `<work-title>`, MuseScore `workTitle`, Guitar Pro `<Title>`.

subtitle.description: A secondary title line. MusicXML `<credit credit-type="subtitle">` (or `<movement-title>` when there is no separate work title), MuseScore `subtitle`, Guitar Pro `<SubTitle>`.

artist.description: The performer this transcription is of (`dc:contributor`) — Guitar Pro's `<Artist>`, the field a tab lists first. Flat rather than a `creators` role because a performer is not a creator of the work; MusicXML has no native home for it and round-trips it as `<creator type="artist">`.

album.description: The release the performance is from. Guitar Pro `<Album>`; MusicXML carries it as a `<miscellaneous-field name="album">`.

creators.description: Who made the work, in source order (`dc:creator`). An array of typed entries rather than one field per role, so an application with a role MNX did not enumerate still has somewhere to put it.

copyright.description: Rights statement as printed (`dc:rights`). MusicXML `<rights>`, MuseScore `copyright`, Guitar Pro `<Copyright>`.

source.description: Where this encoding came from — a URL, a publication, a recording (`dc:source`). MusicXML `<source>`.

notes.description: Free editorial text about the score: performance instructions, provenance, anything the other fields do not name. Guitar Pro `<Instructions>` (with `<Notices>` lines appended); MusicXML `<miscellaneous-field name="notes">`.

encoding.description: What wrote THIS file — the gap w3c-cg/mnx#547 reports from shipping a converter, whose own interim workaround is a vendor `_x` block exactly like this one. Drafts a standard root-level `encoding` object. It describes the MNX file in hand and is stamped by whatever writes it, so it is never copied forward from a source document: an importer replaces it with its own, the way MusicXML's `<encoding>` describes the MusicXML file rather than the file it came from.

software.description: The program that wrote this MNX file. MusicXML `<encoding><software>`, MuseScore `platform`/`programVersion`.

version.description: That program's version, stated separately so a consumer can compare versions without parsing a display string.

date.description: The date it was written, `YYYY-MM-DD` (`dc:date`). MusicXML `<encoding-date>`. Stated as a `pattern` rather than `format: date` because the precompiled validators load no format vocabulary.

note-ext.description: The whole vendor dict at note._x.mnxLab. `string`, `fret` and `fingering` sit flat — peers of the note's own `pitch`/`staff` in the shape they draft — because nesting them under `tab` would make universal fields (fingering is piano's whole interest) fretboard-scoped by construction. A note may carry any subset: `string` alone derives its fret; `fret` alone is meaningless and therefore requires `string`.

part-ext.description: The whole vendor dict at part._x.mnxLab. `strings` declares the sounding pitch of each open string (named to avoid "tuning", which temperament work — w3c-cg/mnx#365 — already claims; the shape mirrors `part.kit` + `kit-note.kitComponent`: declared numbers, referenced by `note._x.mnxLab.string`). ABSENT MEANS NO FINGERBOARD: no consumer assumes an instrument, and tab views are unavailable unless the strings are supplied out-of-band (a viewer-level override — presentation, never written back). Older documents that relied on the retired assume-standard-guitar default are migrated by the load-time shim, which stamps the declaration explicitly.

strings.description: Sounding pitch of each open string, before the capo is applied. Required for any tab rendering — there is no default instrument.

capo.description: Capo fret position (omit or 0 = no capo). Shifts every open-string pitch up by this many semitones AND re-origins printed fret numbers (fret numbers are capo-relative).

global-measure-ext.description: The whole vendor dict at global.measures[i]._x.mnxLab. Harmony lives here — on the GLOBAL timeline beside `key` and `tempos` — because two parts cannot legitimately disagree about the chord on a beat, which is the test that put dynamics and ottavas in the part measure and key/time/tempo in the global one. `rehearsal` and `section` were here in v3; v4 removed them in favour of the standard MNX objects proposed in roadmap/proposed/low-priority/spec-score-text.md — an extension should be a draft of the standard object, so once drafted it stops being an extension.

harmonies.description: Every chord symbol starting in this measure, in `location` order. An array parallel to `tempos` — the other repeatable, metrically-positioned global object.

root-ext.description: The whole vendor dict at the DOCUMENT root — `_x.mnxLab` beside `mnx`, `global` and `parts`. Document metadata lives here, not on a part or a measure, because it is a fact about the whole file: two parts cannot disagree about the title, which is the same test that put key and tempo on the global measure and dynamics on the part measure. `scores[].name` is not this — it names a LAYOUT ("Full score", "Guitar part") and several may exist in one document.
